kill_reason: Not a kill — the absences are genuine. But they are not the binding constraint, so the category verdict is AVAILABILITY_NOT_ASSORTMENT. VERIFIED: 36 of the 60 dairy SKUs that sold in the last 12 months have ZERO stock right now (₹12,06,291 of trailing sales behind an empty shelf); the entire packed-milk shelf for 4,700 people is two live SKUs (Amul Moti 500 ml 484 units, Verka 450 ml 396 units). Worked example, live: 120 units of Smoodh flavoured milk purchased 2026-08-01, 87% sold within 24 hours, sold out 2026-08-05, NOT reordered in the 25 days since. Amul Moti Milk 130 Ml (the ₹10 kids' pouch, 810 u/yr) last purchased 249 days ago; Amul Masti Dahi 85 Gm 309 days; Nestle Every Day 400 Gm (₹42,330/yr, ARY's highest-margin dairy SKU) 97 days. A disciplined availability estimate — 28 already-listed, already-selling SKUs, run-rate annualised over their in-stock days and capped at +100% — is ₹6.81 L/yr of revenue, 2.7× the ₹2.53 L assortment gap, needing no new supplier, no new shelf and no capital. Two further reasons the assortment number stays small: (1) ARY's verified ex-GST dairy margin is 0.6% on Amul Moti 500 ml, −1.3% on Super Dahi 400 g, 2.9% on Amul Butter, 3.1% on cheese slices, and NEGATIVE on the institutional lines (Loose Milk −10.5%, Dahi_Z −8.3%, Desi Ghee 1 L −20.8%) — so even perfect execution earns little; (2) the premium/protein thesis behind most of the research fleet's dairy recommendations is contradicted by ARY's own demand data — the entire health-drink category is ₹54k/yr across ~45 SKUs (₹11 per resident per YEAR), one protein bar sold 24 units, zero whey, while ice cream does ₹13.68 L across 151 selling SKUs. This campus buys frozen sweet dairy, not chilled health dairy.
penetration_assumption: Composite; every line anchored to a comparable SKU ARY already sells, never to a raw % of the 4,700 residents. (a) GENUINELY ABSENT, ₹1,89,020 rev / ₹43,792 GP: full-cream pouch (Amul Gold 500 ml + 1 L) — 27 of the ~300 married-staff households buy one pouch a week for 52 weeks = 1,400 u × ₹38 = ₹53,200 @ 5% (ARY's own demonstrated packed-milk margin, not a book figure); mishti doi 85 g — 33 residents buy one cup a month = 400 u × ₹25 (anchor: Amul Masti Dahi 85 g actually did 252 u/yr) @ 15%; probiotic/lite dahi 400 g — 25 staff/elderly households, one cup a month = 300 u × ₹50 @ 12%; whipping cream 1 L — 8 birthday/bakery cartons a month = 90 u × ₹230 @ 12%; cheese cubes/200 g block — 17 packs a month, 80% of what the 200 g slice pack already does = 200 u × ₹145 @ 12%; lactose-free UHT 1 L — 4 medically-driven households × 2 packs a month = 96 u × ₹95 @ 15%; Greek/fruit yogurt — a 2-SKU TRIAL ONLY at 2 cups a day term-time = 500 u × ₹35 @ 20%, with zero demand evidence, stocked to prove or kill; A2/desi-cow counter tier — 5 L/day for 300 days sold at ₹70 against the existing ₹47 loose tier, incremental ₹23/L = ₹34,500 rev / ₹27,000 GP (this is the one line that is really a REPRICING of milk Purambika already delivers, not a new product). (b) LISTED BUT NEVER PURCHASED, ₹63,900 rev / ₹7,790 GP: curd 1 kg family pack — 25 households × one pack a month × 10 months = 250 u × ₹85 @ 8%; shrikhand 200 g — 150 cups across Gurpurab/Lohri/Baisakhi/Diwali @ 18%; FCMP 500 g — 8 packs a month = 100 u × ₹185 @ 15%; infant formula stage 1-2 — 30 tins/yr × ₹430 @ 10%, carried as duty-of-care for staff families, NOT as an opportunity (IMS Act 1992 bars promoting it). TOTAL ₹2,52,920 rev / ₹51,582 GP, rounded to ₹2.53 L / ₹51,600. Every unit figure above is MY ESTIMATE — the database holds no household count, no comparable-store benchmark and no basket data (97% of bills are the anonymous customer 00001), so the revenue number is the weakest part of this analysis. The prices and margins are VERIFIED; the volumes are not.
probe_evidence: All probes run through a 3-attempt retry harness after discovering a CLI defect (below), and every verdict cross-checked with independent SQL over all 21,479 ProductMaster rows. TRUE ZEROES (probe returned skus_matched=0 on three consecutive attempts, SQL agrees): yogurt / yoghurt / yoghart → 0; greek → 0; epigamia → 0; milky mist → 0; mishti → 0; misti → 0; doi → 0; yakult → 0; nutrifit → 0; prolife → 0; whipping → 0; tropolite → 0; parmesan → 0; feta → 0; gouda → 0; emmental → 0; 'cream cheese' → 0; mozzarella → 0; a2 → 0; 'desi cow' → 0; sahiwal → 0; milkfed → 0; 'full cream' → 0; fullcream → 0; 'full fat' → 0; tetra → 0; uht → 0; skimmed → 0; standardis → 0; buffalo → 0; condens → 0; kalakand → 0; amulspray → 0; similac → 0; dexolac → 0; aptamil → 0; enfamil → 0; farex → 0; nusobee → 0; infant → 0; nandini → 0. FALSE-POSITIVE HITS I CHASED DOWN AND KILLED: 'amul gold' → 27 SKUs, all VESTS in Under Garment (Amul Gold Vest 60 Cm Rn, 25 u/₹875) — Amul Gold milk does not exist here; 'b-activ' → 5 SKUs, all stationery ('Lk Pb-Activity Manual Maths-Tb06'), no Mother Dairy b-Activ; 'probiotic' → 2 SKUs, both Amul Chocobar Probiotic ICE CREAM (₹18,715); 'lactose' → 1 SKU, Amul Lactose Free Vanilla ICE CREAM (₹2,520); 'whip' → 4 SKUs = Snickers Berry Whip ×2 + Nayasa water bottles ×2; 'topping' → 12 SKUs, all pizza/dessert sauces (Dr. Oetker, Veeba, Cremica, Food Coast); 'vacuum' → 3 Nayasa flasks; 'protein' → 12 SKUs = 7 shampoos, Complan, Kelloggs muesli, a Rite Bite bar (24 u sold); 'cheddar' → Veeba Cheesy Melt + Lays chips; 'tofu' → 2 canteen MENU items (Tofu Tikka, Tofu Soya Masala Paneer), 0 sales, no retail SKU. ⚠ TOOL DEFECT FOUND — `ary assort probe` silently returns a 0-row verdict on a transient connection failure: `./ary assort probe lactose cheese` returned skus_matched=0 twice, then 79 on retry, while `probe lactose` (1) and `probe cheese` (78) both worked standalone. A batched loop of probes produced five consecutive false zeroes including 'probiotic' and 'lactose', which independently return hits. Any "missing" verdict produced by a probe loop is unsafe — this is Trap 2 with a new mechanism, and it belongs in Data-Quality-Traps.md.

blockers: REPLENISHMENT IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, and any new SKU inherits it. VERIFIED: 36 of the 60 dairy SKUs that sold in the last 12 months are at zero stock today. Smoodh flavoured milk — 120 u bought 2026-08-01, sold out by 2026-08-05, not reordered in 25 days. Cream Bell Kesar Badam (688 u/yr): 137 days since last purchase. Amul Moti Milk 130 Ml (810 u/yr): 249 days. Amul Masti Dahi 85 Gm (252 u/yr): 309 days. Adding 16 SKU lines to a store that cannot keep 60 on the shelf makes the shelf worse, not better.

MARGIN. Derived from PurchaseDetail.PurchaseCost vs sale realisation, EX-GST on both sides (purchase lines carry IncludeInRate=false with tax separate; sale lines carry IncludeInRate=true — comparing them naively overstates margin by the whole GST wedge, which is how the first pass got 7.9% for Super Dahi instead of −1.3%): Amul Moti 500 ml 0.6%, Super Dahi 400 g −1.3%, Super Dahi 200 g 1.0%, Amul Butter 100 g 2.9%, Amul Cheese Slices 3.1%, Amul Masti Dahi 5.1-5.2%, Verka Milk 450 5.6%. Only loose paneer (16.4%), whitener (15.8%), flavoured milk (15.3%) and Amul Butter MRP-10 (38.8%) pay. ₹2.53 L of new dairy revenue yields ~₹51,600 of gross profit — 0.03% of turnover.

NO DISTRIBUTOR FOR YOGURT. Epigamia, Milky Mist and Mother Dairy chilled do not appear anywhere in the purchase ledger. By contrast Rachna Enterprises and Leela Associates already deliver a wide Amul range (last bills 2026-07-12 and 2026-08-14) and Sahni Trading a deep Verka range (2026-08-01) — so every Amul/Verka gap on this list is an extra line on an invoice that already arrives, while a yogurt shelf is a new supplier relationship into Rajgarh HP.

THE PREMIUM/PROTEIN THESIS IS CONTRADICTED BY ARY'S OWN DEMAND. Whole health-drink category (Bournvita/Horlicks/Complan, ~45 SKUs) = ₹54,000/yr = ₹11 per resident per YEAR. One protein bar sold 24 units. Zero whey. Meanwhile ice cream = ₹13.68 L across 151 selling SKUs, 1.4× the entire chilled dairy shelf. Sizing a Greek-yogurt or protein-lassi opportunity at anything material would be inventing demand for a cohort that has never bought it here.

COLD CHAIN IS NOT A BLOCKER — this needs saying because the demand research assumed it was. Sehgal Trading delivers chilled paneer on 156 bills and Super Dahi on 118/124 bills a year, running to 2026-08-29. ARY holds chillers and freezers (412 active ice-cream SKUs). The constraint is ordering discipline, not refrigeration.

LICENCE. A premium A2/desi-cow counter tier needs an FSSAI source declaration (farm name and location), fat ≥3.5% cow / SNF ≥8.5% verified with a lactometer and fat kit at the counter, food-grade steel cans and annual handler medical certificates. Infant formula cannot be promoted at all under the IMS Act 1992, which is why nine listed Lactogen SKUs have sold 6 tins in their lifetime — carry it, never merchandise it.

STOCK-LEDGER INTEGRITY. Verka Milk 500 Ml shows −10,390 on hand, Curd Btd −547, Amul Butter −17, Verka Pio Elaichi −55. Per the schema identity these negatives are real ledger state, not query artefacts. Any reorder-point automation built on Stock.Quantity will misfire until they are reconciled — and reorder-point automation is what this category actually needs.

CAPITAL IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT — opening stock for all 16 lines is roughly ₹40,000-60,000. Shelf space is not either: 135 of the 195 active dairy SKUs are dormant and 66 of those have never once been purchased, so the facings already exist. The constraint is a buyer who reorders a proven SKU within its shelf life.

FIGURE QUALITY. Prices, margins, stock positions, supplier names and sales are VERIFIED live. Every unit volume in the ₹2.53 L is MY ESTIMATE — the database has no household count, no comparable-store benchmark, and 97% of bills carry no identified buyer (customer 00001), so basket-level validation is impossible. Treat the rupee figure as an order of magnitude, not a forecast.
